chapters.title: Work centers and work center groups
Work center posting and scheduling settings
Work center calendar matrix and capacity calculations

features.name: Work shifts
features.description: Reusable labels assigned to working days in a shop calendar to define shop floor operating hours. Contoso Coffee uses code one for first shift and code two for second shift.

features.name: Shop calendars
features.description: Combine shifts with working days to define when shop floor operates. Support multiple shifts per day and holiday definitions.

features.name: Work center groups
features.description: Higher organizational rank for work centers used for reporting and cost aggregation. Every work center belongs to exactly one group.

features.name: Work center posting settings
features.description: Operational fields on posting tab include direct unit cost, indirect cost percentage, and overhead rate that add to unit cost.

features.name: Work center scheduling configuration
features.description: Scheduling tab allows definition of unit of measure, capacity, efficiency, and shop calendar assignment.

features.name: Machine centers
features.description: Represent individual machines or stations and are always part of a work center. Inherit calendar from parent but have their own capacity, efficiency, and routing setups.

features.name: Consolidated calendar for work centers
features.description: When activated, work center capacity is computed as the sum of its machine centers instead of being defined by the work center card.

features.name: Work center calendar calculation
features.description: Calculate work center calendar to generate capacity matrix showing available production time based on shop calendar, shifts, and holidays.

features.name: Work center calendar matrix
features.description: Shows capacity values in minutes based on shop calendar, including effects of efficiency settings and holidays. Calculates weekly and daily effective capacity.

features.name: Production order scheduling
features.description: System calculates when production must start and finish based on work center capacities, routings, and shop calendar. Accounts for maintenance windows and non-working days.

quotes.text: On Business Central, by clicking into capacities, you can access work centers, machine centers, and related setup pages that drives production scheduling.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the core objects and pages available in the capacity model entry point in Business Central.

quotes.text: Work shifts are the smallest building blocks. Contoso has two shifts, code one for the first shift, and code two for the second shift.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes work shifts as the foundational building block of capacity definition.

quotes.text: A work center using two shifts can schedule 16 hours per day instead of eight.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the practical impact of shift configuration on available production capacity.

quotes.text: Every work center belongs to exactly one group and are useful for costing.
quotes.why_it_matters: Defines the mandatory relationship between work centers and groups with costing purpose.

quotes.text: Our weekly capacity the work center 200 is 2,400 minutes of effective capacity.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows how calendar matrix quantifies capacity in minutes for scheduling.

quotes.text: Once we click refresh production order, the system calculates when production must start and finish.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the mechanism by which production orders are scheduled against capacity.

quotes.text: Business Central uses calendar entries for scheduling your production against your capacities.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the role of calendar entries in the scheduling algorithm.
